title: Granite Query
subtitle: Learning More from Less
research_question: Can student aware data selection help Granite learn mathematical reasoning from DeepSeek more efficiently than random selection?
next_action: Await user review of the completed pilot; no additional paid jobs are queued.
caveat: Teacher pilot uses training questions. It is not held-out accuracy or evidence of Granite improvement.

events.title: Smoke-test results are not benchmark accuracy
events.detail: All 12 optimizer updates completed and adapter parameters changed. The saved adapter reloaded and all three development answers matched their reference numbers. Baseline responses were limited to 192 tokens and two were visibly truncated, so this tiny comparison cannot establish accuracy improvement. Preserve these outputs and use an adequate shared generation budget in the controlled experiment.

One seed; equal example counts, with actual token counts reported. Reserved 3 dollars DeepSeek and 3 dollars Modal. No official test data.

events.title: Interpretation audit identified selection confounds
events.detail: The first comparison matches 32 examples and optimizer updates, but selected solution lengths and training order differ. Ranked examples are trained in BM25 order while random examples are shuffled. Development question text also contributed to the pre-existing reference index statistics, though development answers and outcomes were not ranking inputs. Report these limits, preserve the frozen run, and avoid claiming that ranking alone caused any difference.

events.title: First ranked versus random run completed
events.detail: Numeric development matches out of 16: baseline 13, ranked 13, random 13. Supervised training tokens: ranked 3260, random 2534. Both adapters and raw evaluations saved. One seed and development data only; no final-test or robust generalization claim.

events.title: Comparison results independently audited
events.detail: Original Granite, BM25 selected, and random selected each scored 13 of 16. All 48 outputs have plain numeric final answers and no truncation. Ranked fixes one baseline error but introduces another; random has the same correctness pattern as baseline. Ranked used 3260 supervised tokens versus 2534 for random, about 28.65 percent more. No ranking accuracy or fixed-token efficiency advantage is demonstrated. One ambiguous benchmark item is retained under the frozen scoring policy.

events.title: Further paid expansion stopped pending review
events.detail: Both adapters and evaluation outputs are preserved. The first comparison is complete. A confirmatory run should match token budgets, use the same shuffled order policy, exclude development questions from relevance-index fitting, and repeat across seeds. No additional GPU jobs are queued.

limitations: One seed and 16 training-split development questions.
Equal examples and updates, not equal supervised training tokens.
Selection and training order are entangled.
Development question text contributed to the fixed BM25 index corpus statistics; development answers and outcomes were not used in ranking.
Numeric extraction is heuristic and does not grade explanation quality.
Latency is exploratory: sequential evaluation without repeated randomized timing.
